data.description:
v2AwaitCallback's main-thread branch cannot receive a callback delivered on the main dispatch queue. WKWebView.evaluateJavaScript delivers completion handlers exactly that way, so EVERY browser JS eval reaching that branch is guaranteed to fail: it burns its full timeout, then returns nil. While burning it, it holds the main queue — and socket commands reach their work via v2MainSync — so each failing browser command freezes the entire CLI/socket control plane and the UI for the full timeout.

Code is BYTE-IDENTICAL at v0.61.0 (the build that wedged) and release/v0.64.0 (current). Not a stale-build problem — it ships today. Blocks next production release.

PROVEN by repro harness at tools/await-wedge-repro/ (run.sh):
  timer     (CFRunLoop timer source)        -> callback FIRES,      0.50s
  mainqueue (DispatchQueue.main.async)      -> callback NEVER runs, 3.00s -> nil
  never     (never invoked)                 -> 3.00s -> nil
Same code, same nesting, only delivery path differs. A nested CFRunLoopRunInMode inside an in-progress _dispatch_main_queue_drain cannot drain main-queue blocks; libdispatch will not re-enter a drain already on the stack.

This falsifies the shipped comment at BrowserHandlers.swift:321-324 ('The loop still pumps events (WebKit completion callbacks, rendering, main-queue blocks), so main is not frozen'). Those are precisely what it does NOT pump.

PRODUCTION INCIDENT 2026-08-12: ~53-agent Marquee V2 fleet running browser-proof gates. Main thread stalled 25+ min continuous and monotonic, longest fleet timeout 60s. UI dead, every c11 CLI call died at its 10s client timeout, event stream froze. Agents themselves unaffected (28/53 measurably advancing, PTYs draining). Immune to killing the WebContent process (termination error is itself main-queue delivered) and to lldb (hardened runtime + SIP).

REAL-WORLD RATE, agent transcripts 2026-08-12: 205 'timeout: method=browser' + 29 'Condition not met before timeout' + 3 'Timed out waiting for JavaScript result' = 237 failures in one day. CLI abandons at 10s while server keeps burning its timeout, so these are largely invisible in ps and read as agent flakiness.

NOT YET EXPLAINED: repro shows the deadline loop DOES unwind on time, so one stuck await cannot explain a 25-min stall. Leading hypothesis is a serialized backlog of failing commands (agents retry after 10s CLI timeout, refilling faster than drain). SIGSTOPing all 55 agents for 4 min did not drain it — likely too short for a 20-min backlog, but unconfirmed. NEXT STEP: freeze all agents 20-30 min and watch stalledMs. Plateau = backlog confirmed and wedge is self-healing given quiet; still climbing with zero agents = a second defect.

FIXES:
1. Do not await a main-queue-delivered callback from inside a main-queue drain. Keep the JS-eval await off the main-thread branch, or make the socket command complete asynchronously instead of blocking main. Root fix; rest is mitigation.
2. Cap timeout_ms (BrowserHandlers.swift:1357 is lower-bounded only: max(1, ... ?? 5_000)). Uncapped value is a direct multiplier on control-plane downtime.
3. Correct the comment at BrowserHandlers.swift:321-324 — it documents behavior the implementation lacks.
4. Fail fast when the WKWebView has no committed document instead of burning the timeout.

RELATED, BOTH UNMERGED (in neither main nor release/v0.64.0) — assess together before release:
  origin/fix/C11-198-runloop-idle  'stops swallowing nested run loops' (2026-08-10)
  origin/fix/C11-204-modal-wedge   'browser modals never go app-modal' (2026-08-11); per CLAUDE.md the insecure-HTTP prompt held main up to 6.8h. Fleet drives proofs against http://127.0.0.1, exactly that path.

INSTRUMENTATION: MainThreadHangMonitor worked well (C11-192 fingerprinting attributed the stall correctly). Two gaps: hang.log grew ~23MB/min to 212MB (needs rotation/cap; ~1.3GB/hr sustained), and seven precursor episodes (2.4s-10.7s) never surfaced to the operator — a repeated-fingerprint signal would have flagged this before it went terminal.

Full writeup: docs/c11-browser-await-main-wedge.md
data.title: Browser JS await starves the main queue — wedges socket control plane and UI

data.body:
CORRECTION + scope narrowed after testing against a real WKWebView.

My original claim — 'EVERY browser JS eval reaching the main-thread branch is guaranteed to fail' — was WRONG. It rested on a harness that modeled delivery with DispatchQueue.main.async. WebKit does not deliver that way; it hops IPC replies onto the main RUNLOOP, which the nested pump DOES service.

Real WKWebView matrix (tools/await-wedge-repro/WebKitDelivery.swift, 3.0s timeout):
  loaded       (document committed)               -> fires, 0.05s
  deadport     (load issued, connection refused)  -> fires, 0.05s
  hanging      (server accepts, never responds)   -> fires, 0.05s
  uncommitted  (NO load ever issued)              -> NEVER fires, 3.09s -> nil

The defect is real but NARROW: it needs a WKWebView that has never been asked to load anything (no assigned web process). Then evaluateJavaScript's completion never fires and the await burns its full uncapped timeout_ms while holding the main queue — freezing the whole socket control plane and UI.

deadport and hanging — the intuitive suspects — both resolve fine. A 'url == nil' guard would NOT distinguish them: deadport also reports url=nil, isLoading=false after failure. Fix #2 needs real commit-state tracking on BrowserPanel (didStartProvisionalNavigation/didCommit).

Corroboration from the incident: WebContent PID 1400, spawned at exactly 18:27:44 alongside the surface, had opened ZERO page resources — signature of a prewarmed process never assigned a document, matching the uncommitted case.

The DispatchQueue.main.async finding still stands as a latent hazard: libdispatch will not re-enter a drain already on the stack, so anything added to this path later that delivers via the main queue will silently burn its full timeout. Keep fix #4 (correct the comment at BrowserHandlers.swift:321-324).

Also correcting my earlier note on related work: C11-204 (#417) and C11-198 (#413) ARE merged and DO ship in release/v0.64.0 / PR #419 — I had checked raw feature-branch SHAs, which differ from squash-merge SHAs. The 6.8h modal wedge IS fixed in this release. C11-209 is not.

Release-gating call: still a genuine control-plane freeze, but it requires browser wait/eval against a never-navigated surface, and the c11 skill already advises navigating first. Recommend fix #1 (cap timeout_ms) as the cheap bounded mitigation and fix #3 (off-main via socketWorkerV2Methods — the same remedy C11-26 applied to the terminal path, see waitForTerminalSurfaceOffMain) as the root fix with a real test pass, NOT on a release branch.

Full corrected writeup: docs/c11-browser-await-main-wedge.md

data.body:
# C11-209 — phase-4 validation evidence

Tagged build `c11-209` from this worktree (branch head at validation time: `4399a8dd5`),
launched via `./scripts/reload.sh --tag c11-209` with `C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh`, driven through
the tagged socket `/tmp/c11-debug-c11-209.sock` exactly as an agent would.

Surface under test: `surface:6`, created with `c11 new-surface --type browser --pane pane:3`
and **never navigated** (`get url` returns empty) — the production trigger.

## The probe question first

Per plan resolution R1, `c11 ping` is NOT a main-thread probe: `socketWorkerImmediateV1Response`
answers it on the socket worker before any main hop. The probe used throughout is
`c11 tree --no-layout`, which takes the default main-actor policy.

**I proved the probe rather than assuming it.** Positive control, on a *loaded* page with a
condition that can never be met, which still holds main by design:

```
$ c11 browser surface:6 wait --text-contains zzzz-never-present --timeout-ms 20000 &
$ sleep 2; time c11 tree --no-layout
c11 tree --no-layout   0.02s user 0.01s system 0% cpu 10.028 total     <-- STALLED (hit the CLI's 10s deadline)
$ time c11 ping
PONG
c11 ping               0.01s user 0.01s system 12% cpu 0.142 total     <-- FAST, during the same wedge
```

So: `c11 tree` genuinely detects a held main thread, and `c11 ping` genuinely does not. Every
"fast tree" result below is therefore meaningful, and R1's concern is now measured, not just
read off the source.

## Matrix

| # | probe | result | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | never-loaded surface, `wait --load-state complete --timeout-ms 120000` | `no_document` in **0.141s** (vs 120s requested) | PASS |
| V2 | never-loaded surface, `eval "1+1"` | `no_document` in **0.141s** | PASS |
| V3 | `goto https://example.com`, then `eval "1+1"` | `{"value": 2}` in 0.192s | PASS |
| V4 | loaded page, `wait --load-state complete --timeout-ms 30000` | `OK` in 0.193s | PASS |
| V5 | loaded page, `wait --text-contains <absent> --timeout-ms 20000` | timeout at **20.151s** — legitimate long waits are NOT truncated | PASS |
| V6a | `download wait --path … --timeout-ms 30000`, file arrives at t+3s | `OK` at **3.185s** | PASS |
| V6b | same, nothing ever arrives | timeout at **15.147s** for a 15s request — deadline honoured, no hang | PASS |
| V7 | loaded page, unmet condition, `--timeout-ms 600000` | returns at **120.03s**, payload `{"timeout_ms":120000,"requested_timeout_ms":600000}` | PASS |
| V8 | `c11 tree --no-layout` concurrent with V1 | **0.143s** | PASS |
| V9 | `c11 ping` concurrent with V1 | 0.139s — recorded to document that this probe is vacuous | n/a |

V7 raw socket response (bypassing the CLI's error formatting, to show the data payload):

```
elapsed=120.03s
{"id":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"timeout","message":"Condition not met before timeout",
 "data":{"timeout_ms":120000,"requested_timeout_ms":600000}}}
```

V6a is the direct proof of the off-main delivery fix. Before it, `browser.download.wait`'s
file-system source was created with `queue: .main` and therefore could never fire inside the
nested pump, so this exact probe would have run the full 30s instead of 3.185s.

## Before-column

Per the delegator brief ("measure on origin/main first if cheap, or cite the harness"), the
before-behaviour is cited from `tools/await-wedge-repro/`, re-run on this machine at the start
of the ticket rather than inherited from the writeup:

```
WebKitDelivery.swift, 3.0s timeout, real WKWebView
  loaded       document committed                      fired      0.05s
  deadport     load issued, connection refused          fired      0.05s
  uncommitted  NO LOAD EVER ISSUED                      NEVER     3.12s -> nil

AwaitDeadlock.swift, 3.0s timeout, synthetic delivery
  timer        CFRunLoop timer source                   fired      0.53s   (8 pump slices)
  mainqueue    DispatchQueue.main.async                 NEVER     3.01s    (1,566,040 slices)
  never        never invoked                            no        3.01s    (3,165,821 slices)
```

The `uncommitted` row is V1/V2's before-state: the await burns its full `timeout_ms` holding
main. The `mainqueue` row is V6a's before-state. The slice counts show the failing case also
busy-spins a core for the whole window.

## Health after the full matrix

```
tagged app ALIVE
c11 ping -> PONG
c11 tree --no-layout -> 0.141s
"BUG IN CLIENT OF LIBDISPATCH" in last 15m: 0
new c11 crash reports: none
```

The libdispatch check matters specifically: the download-wait rework moved the watched file
descriptor's lifetime into the `DispatchSource` cancel handler, and getting that wrong is a
trap, not a silent leak. V6a/V6b exercised both the early-resolution and deadline-unwind exit
paths with no trap.

## What was NOT validated end-to-end, and why

- **The duplicate-download-event fix** (review MINOR #2 — the event queue is now the single
  source of truth). The path-based branch of `download wait` does not read that queue, and the
  notification branch needs a real `WKDownload`, which I could not trigger from the socket. The
  change is code-level and reviewed; it is not covered by the matrix above and I am not
  claiming it is.
- **The `didStartProvisionalNavigation` belt** is exercised implicitly by V3/V4 (navigation
  succeeds and subsequent JS works), not by a dedicated probe.

## Observation, pre-existing, not introduced here

`download wait --path` watches the *parent directory*, and `pathIsReady()` requires
`size > 0`. A file created empty and then written in place produces one directory event (at
create, when size is still 0) and no further directory event for the data write, so the wait
can time out even though the file eventually appears. V6a passes because it uses the
atomic-rename pattern (`mv` into place), which is also what a real download does. This
behaviour is unchanged by C11-209 — before the fix the source could not fire at all — but it
is worth a follow-up ticket.
